citations.assessment: The directly checked Bavli names Yishmael son of Yose in the illness account, while Heilprin gives Shimon and reports Yishmael in Ein Yaakov. Preserve this as a witnessed difference.
The checked digital witness exposes a first-speaker variant and names Yishmael rather than Shimon son of Yose in the alternative. The printed Heilprin witness should remain visible.
The checked Bavli also has Yishmael here, like the Ran report, rather than the Shimon name printed by Heilprin.
Ran explicitly names Yishmael son of Yose and gives competing precise construals of the wife’s vow conditions.
Direct witness has Shimon son of Yose in Shimon’s name on the qualification for bringing a sacrifice for error.
The direct witness gives Rav Huna in the name of Yishmael son of Yose in the alternate report about a remnant.
Shimon son of Yose directly reports in his father’s name on the quantity of cleaning stones.
The preceding article supplies the exact name that motivates Heilprin’s proposed identification; keep it tentative.
The direct digital Ein Yaakov in the tenth chapter gives Yishmael in the illness account, as does the checked Bavli. Keep Heilprin’s distinct reporting of their readings.
The explicit name in the Ein Yaakov clause points to the matching Yishmael article.

holds.raw: ואולי ר' שמעון בר' יוסי אלו
holds.reason: The internal Lakunya pointer is exact. Its proposed application across the set of Shimon reports remains conjectural given the differing names in the checked passages.

holds.raw: כי לר' יוסי בר"ח לא היה לו בן שמעון
holds.reason: Shabbat 118b lists five sons without a Shimon, which is evidence for Heilprin’s contrast. Historical exhaustiveness and identification of these reports remain open.
The checked end-of-Pekudei Yalkut witnesses did not locate an exact Shimon son of Yose text for the brief notice. Preserve the citation and distinguish this bounded lookup from absence.
